thread:
linda: Heads up — we need to finalize alerting rules for the new runtime dashboards (kv cache, batch size, tail-latency). Can eng-platform + runtime collaborate on thresholds and PD mapping? We have a canary rollout next Tue.

sarah: On it. Can you list which metrics you'll be surfacing? I'd like to propose per-model + global thresholds.

ajay: From runtime side: metric names we export are `runtime_kv_cache_hit_ratio`, `runtime_batch_size_p50`, `runtime_batch_size_p95`, `runtime_token_latency_p99`, and `runtime_retries_total`. They have labels: `pool`, `model`, `region`. All shipped to prometheus via metrics-forwarder.

mike: Quick take — avoid noisy p50 alerts. Recommend paging on sustained p99 latency and sustained KV-hit drops. Example: p99 > 200ms for 10m OR KV hit ratio drop >10% sustained for 5m. Also tie to SLO burn-rate alert (6h window). Pager routing: primary -> eng-runtime, fallback -> eng-sre.

linda: +1. Can someone draft the alert rules YAML so we can iterate? I'll add runbook links and PD IDs once the rules settle.

ajay: Draft below, please review:
```yaml
groups:
- name: runtime_alerts
  rules:
  - alert: RuntimeTokenLatencyHigh
    expr: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(runtime_token_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le, model, pool)) > 0.2
    for: 10m
    labels:
      severity: page
      team: eng-runtime
    annotations:
      summary: "p99 token latency > 200ms for {{ $labels.model }}"
      runbook: https://redwood/runbooks/runtime/p99-latency
  - alert: KVCacheHitDrop
    expr: avg_over_time(runtime_kv_cache_hit_ratio[10m]) < 0.85
    for: 5m
    labels:
      severity: page
      team: eng-runtime
    annotations:
      summary: "runtime_kv_cache_hit_ratio dropped below 85% for {{ $labels.pool }}"
      runbook: https://redwood/runbooks/runtime/kv-cache-drop
```

sarah: That looks good. From console side we should surface these alerts on the new dashboard and add an opt-in subscription per-route. Default: enabled for critical models, opt-out for low-traffic. UX: small toggle on each route panel + a global alerts page.

ajay: For SLO burn rate we plan to emit `slo_burn_rate{route,model}`. Quick test query for a 6h burn: `increase(slo_error_budget_consumed_total[6h]) / 6` (we'll normalize per-hour). We can also compute a heatmap in the dashboard.

mike: PD mapping notes: primary policy `P-ENG-RUNTIME` (PD ID P12345), fallback `P-ENG-SRE` (PD ID P23456). Add dedupe by normalizing `model` label so we don't page multiple times for same fault across compatible models. Also enforce a 5m grouping window.

linda: Action items:
- ajay -> push prometheus rules PR by EOD Thu (include runbook links + labels).
- sarah -> Console subscription UX mock by Mon (annotate canary window).
- mike -> create PD escalation policies and a runbook template (include mute window plan).
- linda -> schedule dry-run during canary and collect PD IDs. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: deploy-bot: New prometheus rules PR #112 created by ajay — CI checks passing. Link: https://git/repo/pr/112

ajay: I'll add a synthetic traffic job to generate p99 pressure and verify alerts trigger before the canary. Test probe example: `ab -n 10000 -c 50 http://canary.example/v1/generate` (we'll replace with internal harness).

sarah: On dashboards I'll add: p99 latency line chart, rolling 6h burn-rate heatmap, per-pool KV hit ratio with warning coloring, and an annotations layer for canary windows.

mike: One more: define explicit mute windows for the canary and planned maintenance. Use PD schedules and annotate the dashboard so ops knows to ignore expected blips.

linda: Perfect. I'll collect the PD IDs and post final doc here by Fri noon. If no blockers we aim to merge rules PR 24h before canary. Thanks everyone!
